newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown extends gains on mark.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown extends gains on mark.

text.p: The Czech crown continued on Thursday to take advantage of problems with its reference currency, the mark, firming further as better-than-expected Czech trade figures kept the Prague market humming.

The crown firmed to 18.706 after 18.772 late Wednesday and 19.009 at Wednesday's open. Dealers said the combination of the mark's weakening against the dollar and the trade figures had several Prague players moving out of the mark.
"The move from yesterday was quite surprising. After the (trade) figures...it was obvious the Czech crown could strengthen on the mark again," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.
The Czech June trade gap narrowed to 9.6 billion crowns from 11.0 in May, data released on Tuesday revealed, contributing to a slow but consistent firming of the Czech currency.
The crown was trading on Thursday about 12.3 percent below its February peak against the mark, but only about 3.4 percent below the level just before it was floated on May 27.
"There have been some players on the market caught long on hard currency, and that's maybe the reason for the Czech crown strengthening today," Korous said.
The crown remained steady against the dollar at 34.218, as the greenback held its gains on the German currency.
Dealers said they saw the crown's new support at 18.700 with resistence at 18.835-860, but the market was already testing the basement at around 1.30 p.m. (1130 gmt).
However analysts have cautioned that while the Czech June trade figures got a boost from the weaker crown, flooding in the eastern part of the country could reverse the trend.

One dealer said that Czech central bank, after pushing up interest rates to defend the crown and then bringing them gradually down in recent weeks, may have run out of room to ease rates further, and would instead now concentrate on keeping inflation in check.
Still, the longer-term outlook on the crown was that it still had room to weaken, if the German mark recovers from its current problems.
